transcript: I love a family drama on Broadway, especially when it’s as blistering and hilarious as Purpose by Branden Jacobs-Jenkins. This new play revolves around the prominent Jasper family, which with an influence spanning from the Civil Rights Movement to contemporary politics, has long been a symbol of Black excellence. But, like with every family, there are skeletons in the closet which cause all sorts of mayhem over the course of one eventful weekend. It's always a privilege to see Kara Young on stage, though the entire cast is spectacular, as is the direction by Phylicia Rashad. This play has some similarities to Appropriate, the last piece by Branden Jacobs-Jenkins seen on Broadway. I'd say the most obvious ones are the well-rendered characters and family dynamics, the effortlessly natural yet poetic writing, and the bitingly funny conflicts and surprises throughout. Thematically, Purpose is very different, and the way it intricately layers ideas about identity politics and contemporary Black experiences with themes seen in many family dramas such as legacy and familial resentments, makes for a richly complex but entertaining and accessible piece. If I were on the Pulitzer committee, this play would absolutely be in consideration. With that, another playbill for my collection.
